tool.name: WMTS_to_MBTiles

param.name: wmts_url
param.dialogReference:
URL pointing to the WMTS capabilities document (WMTSCapabilities.xml).

For example: https://services.arcgisonline.com/arcgis/rest/services/World_Imagery/MapServer/WMTS/1.0.0/WMTSCapabilities.xml
param.pythonReference:
URL pointing to the WMTS capabilities document (WMTSCapabilities.xml).

For example: https://services.arcgisonline.com/arcgis/rest/services/World_Imagery/MapServer/WMTS/1.0.0/WMTSCapabilities.xml

param.name: wmts_layer
param.dialogReference:
Layer identifier parsed from the capabilities file. This should pull through from the dropdown once the WMTS Capabilities URL is entered.

The tool only works with EPSG 3857 (Web Mercator).

Example: World_Imagery
param.pythonReference:
Layer identifier parsed from the capabilities file. This should pull through from the dropdown once the WMTS Capabilities URL is entered.

The tool only works with EPSG 3857 (Web Mercator).

Example: World_Imagery

param.name: extent_fc
param.dialogReference:
Polygon feature class or shapefile defining the geographic area to download.

This must be in EPSG 3857.

The polygon feature class must be selected by clicking the folder icon in the tool.
param.pythonReference:
Polygon feature class or shapefile defining the geographic area to download.

This must be in EPSG 3857.

The polygon feature class must be selected by clicking the folder icon in the tool.

param.name: crop_to_extent
param.displayname: Crop Metadata Extent to Input Area
param.dialogReference:
If checked (the default), the MBTiles 'bounds' metadata field is set to the tight bounding box of your Extent Feature Class (in WGS84 lon/lat, as the MBTiles spec requires). If unchecked, no 'bounds' field is written.

Note: this only affects descriptive metadata some viewers use for 'zoom to layer' or panning limits. It does NOT crop or renumber the actual tiles.
param.pythonReference:
If checked (the default), the MBTiles 'bounds' metadata field is set to the tight bounding box of your Extent Feature Class (in WGS84 lon/lat, as the MBTiles spec requires). If unchecked, no 'bounds' field is written.

Note: this only affects descriptive metadata some viewers use for 'zoom to layer' or panning limits. It does NOT crop or renumber the actual tiles.

param.name: min_zoom
param.dialogReference:
Lowest zoom level to download (0-19).

Lower zoom = fewer tiles.
param.pythonReference:
Lowest zoom level to download (0-19).

Lower zoom = fewer tiles.

param.name: max_zoom
param.dialogReference:
Highest zoom level to download (0-19).

Higher zoom = more tiles, larger MBTiles. Each extra zoom level makes the file roughly four times larger.
param.pythonReference:
Highest zoom level to download (0-19).

Higher zoom = more tiles, larger MBTiles. Each extra zoom level makes the file roughly four times larger.

param.name: output_mbtiles
param.dialogReference: Path and name of the MBTiles file (.mbtiles) to create. An existing file with the same name is overwritten.
param.pythonReference: Path and name of the MBTiles file (.mbtiles) to create. An existing file with the same name is overwritten.

tool.summary:
Downloads tiles from a WMTS service and packages them into an MBTiles file suitable for offline use in applications such as ATAK/WinTAK, QGIS, SITAWARE and Skydio X10D Handsets.

Supports WMTS Capabilities parsing, GoogleMapsCompatible tile matrix sets, retry logic for unstable servers and high-zoom tile extraction. Tested with Esri World Imagery, GeoServer WMTS, MapProxy WMTS and RBT WMTS.
tool.usage:
Do NOT use ArcGIS geoprocessing environments with this tool. The tool manages its own workspace, projection, and tile maths.

The Extent Feature Class must be in EPSG 3857 (Web Mercator). If you see NaN tile math errors, define or project the extent to EPSG:3857.

Server errors such as 502s and DNS failures are retried automatically.

ATAK: copy the MBTiles file into internal storage\atak\imagery (no subfolders) and restart ATAK. WinTAK: copy it into C:\ProgramData\WinTAK\Imagery (no subfolders) and restart WinTAK.
